Issues.Title: fix(compiler): preserve entity-decoded spaces in template text
Issues.Body:
## Description With `preserveWhitespaces: false` (the default), entity-decoded Unicode spaces are treated as insignificant whitespace: - `WS_CHARS` includes `\u2000-\u200a` and `\u205f`, so a text node containing only ` ` / ` ` / ` ` is considered blank and removed, runs collapse to an ASCII space, and boundary occurrences are trimmed. - The boundary trimming uses `String#trimStart` / `#trimEnd`, which also remove `\u00A0`, contradicting the `WS_CHARS` comment that excludes NBSP. `
 hello 
` currently produces `"hello"`; it should produce `"\u2003hello\u2003"`. ## Fix - Drop `\u2000-\u200a` and `\u205f` from `WS_CHARS`. - Trim with `^[WS_CHARS]+` / `[WS_CHARS]+$` regexes instead of `String#trimStart/#trimEnd` at all four sites. ASCII whitespace handling is unchanged: `
hello
` still trims to `"hello"` and `
a b
` still collapses to `"a b"`. ## Tests Added to `html_whitespaces_spec.ts` for the `preserveWhitespaces: false` path: ` ` alone, boundaries around text, repeated ` `, ` `, plus ASCII trimming/collapsing controls. Verified by bundling the actual `packages/compiler/src/ml_parser` sources with esbuild and running `removeWhitespaces(ast, false)` under Node 24. The Jasmine/Bazel suite was not run because this checkout has no Bazel toolchain. Fixes #24217.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): preserve entity-decoded spaces in template text" (#71559)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): avoid conflicting namespace imports in CopySourceToTcb shims
Issues.Body:
In CopySourceToTcb mode, inline type-check ops and the type-check file itself use separate ImportManagers that both generate aliases i0, i1, ... into the same shim, so one alias could refer to two different modules, causing false signal-input errors in the language service. The imports inserted into the copied source were also concatenated without a separator, which made the shim unparseable.

The copied-source ops now use a distinct `_i` namespace prefix and each inserted import ends with a newline. Verified with a new spec that fails without the fix, plus the typecheck, language-service and ngtsc suites.

Fixes #71547
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): avoid conflicting namespace imports in CopySourceToTcb shims" (#71558)

Issues.Title: perf(core): avoid unnecessary aborts and reuse abort reason during resource teardown
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [x] Other... Please describe: Performance optimization

## What is the current behavior?

When tearing down a view tree containing resources (e.g. during route navigation), `ResourceImpl.destroy()` invokes `abortInProgressLoad()`, calling `pendingController.abort()` without arguments.

This leads to significant teardown latency due to two factors:
1. Per the WHATWG DOM spec, calling `abort()` with no reason instantiates a new `"AbortError"` `DOMException`. In V8/Chromium, `DOMException` construction triggers `v8::Exception::CaptureStackTrace()`. The cost of walking execution stack frames scales linearly with call stack depth (~140 µs per call at depth 300 on throttled CPUs). When destroying dozens of resources in deep view trees, this adds 20–40ms of main thread blockage.
2. `ResourceImpl` retains its `pendingController` even after a one-shot (non-streaming) loader has settled (resolved or errored). When the component is eventually destroyed, `abort()` is executed on controllers whose operations finished long ago.

Issue Number: #71422

## What is the new behavior?

1. **Reused Abort Reason**:
   `abortInProgressLoad()` now passes a shared, lazily-initialized `DOMException('The operation was aborted.', 'AbortError')`. Passing an existing `DOMException` prevents V8 from capturing a fresh call stack on every call while preserving complete Web API and consumer compatibility (`err.name === 'AbortError'`, `err instanceof DOMException`).
2. **Clear Pending Controller on Completion**:
   For non-streaming resources (`PromiseResourceOptions`), once the loader promise settles (in `finally`), `pendingController` is cleared if it belongs to that settled load. When the resource is destroyed later, teardown does not perform unnecessary abort work or event dispatch. Streaming resources (like `rxResource` or `StreamingResourceOptions`) retain their controller so active subscriptions and streams continue to be cleanly aborted on destroy.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Draft PR proposing the two-pronged optimization discussed in #71422 and #71423.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "perf(core): avoid unnecessary aborts and reuse abort reason during resource teardown" (#71557)

Issues.Title: docs(forms): update stale statements in the signal forms API docs
Issues.Body:
- PACKAGE.md: debouncing is supported through the `debounce()` rule, so remove it from the list of unsupported features.
- Use the `{when}` form of `disabled()` in JSDoc examples instead of the deprecated function overload.

Issues.Title: docs(forms): show the validator message for compat errors in the migration guide
Issues.Body: The compat example rendered `error.message || error.kind`, but errors from existing reactive validators are `CompatValidationError`s, which don't set `message`. The example showed the error key ("enterprisePassword") instead of the validator's message. Read the message from the error's `context` for compat errors.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs(forms): show the validator message for compat errors in the migration guide" (#71554)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): add explicit preprocessor analyzer options alongside tsconfig
Issues.Body:
The preprocessor analyzer could only be configured by reading a tsconfig, which prevents integrations (bundlers, the Angular CLI) that have no tsconfig or already own the parsed configuration from driving it directly. This is the first step toward making the analyzer tsconfig-agnostic.

Every setting that was previously only read from the tsconfig is now also an explicit `AnalyzerOptions` field: `strictStandalone`, `strictInjectionParameters`, `compileNonExportedClasses` and `generateExtraImportsInLocalMode`. Settings that only configure the built-in file-system module resolution move into a separate `defaultHost` (`rootDirs`, `preserveSymlinks`, `nodeModulesPathOverride`), since they will belong to the default host rather than the analyzer core once resolution is delegated to a host. `importPrefixRoots` replaces the ambiguously named `rootDirs` option, which only ever configured the `PrefixImportStrategy` roots. The previous `rootDirs` and top-level `nodeModulesPathOverride` fields remain as deprecated aliases.

All new fields are optional and fall back to the tsconfig; an explicitly set option always wins. Construction is split into `EffectiveConfig::resolve`, the single place where options are merged over tsconfig values, and `Analyzer::construct`, which preserves the previous construction order. Behavior is unchanged when no new options are set.

`LoadAnalyzerOptions` now extends the engine's `AnalyzerOptions` and the loader forwards engine options as-is instead of copying a fixed subset of fields, so new engine options are usable through `createAnalyzer()` without loader changes. `SidecarAnalyzer.initialize` forwards any additional engine options the same way.

Issues.Title: fix(router): don't intercept downloads and POST forms with the Navigation API
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

With `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`, `<a download>` links and POST form submissions under the app's base href are converted to SPA navigations. Their `navigate` events have `canIntercept: true`, and `handleNavigate` only lets reloads and non-interceptable events through. The file is never downloaded and the form data is never sent.

Issue Number: Fixes #71551

## What is the new behavior?

`handleNavigate` also returns early when the event has a `downloadRequest` or `formData`, the same way it does for reloads. GET form submissions don't carry `formData`, so they're still converted to SPA navigations. Both are compared to `null` rather than checked for truthiness: `downloadRequest` is an empty string for `<a download>` without a file name, which is what the links on angular.dev use.

The tests are in the "real platform navigation" block of `with_platform_navigation.spec.ts`, because `FakeNavigation` always sets both properties to `null`. They click a real `<a download>` and submit a real POST form, cancel the event after the router's listener so the test browser doesn't download or submit anything, and check that the router didn't start a navigation. Both fail without the fix: the router emits `NavigationStart` for `/file.txt` and `/submit`. A third test checks that a GET form still becomes an SPA navigation.

I also tried it in a small app built against 22.2.1: with the check added, the link downloads the file and the server receives the POST.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(router): don't intercept downloads and POST forms with the Navigation API" (#71552)

Issues.Title: Router intercepts `<a download>` links and POST form submissions with `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? router ### Is this a regression? No ### Description With `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`, the router intercepts every same-origin `navigate` event under the app's base href, except reloads. That includes two kinds of navigations it can't handle: - ``: the event has `downloadRequest` set and `canIntercept: true`. The router turns it into an SPA navigation to `/report.csv`, and the file is never downloaded. - `
`: the event has `formData` set and `canIntercept: true`. The router navigates to `/submit` inside the app, and the POST request is never sent. Without the feature, both work as expected, since the router only handles clicks on `RouterLink`. GET forms are fine either way: they don't carry `formData`, and turning them into SPA navigations is the point of the feature. angular.dev hits the first case since #71504. On next.angular.dev (22.3.0-next.2+sha-16932e9), the download links on [/ai/develop-with-ai](https://next.angular.dev/ai/develop-with-ai) (`` and the ones in the table below it) open the "Page Not Found" page instead of downloading the file. #71504 is on 22.2.x too, so angular.dev will get the same behavior with its next deployment. `NavigationStateManager.handleNavigate` returns early when `canIntercept` is false or when `navigationType` is `'reload'` (added in dbd50be7f7 for #66746), but doesn't check `downloadRequest` or `formData`. The `shouldNotIntercept` example in the Chrome article linked from the `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation` docs leaves both of them to the browser. #71552 leaves both to the browser. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction, but this is self-contained: ```ts import {Component} from '@angular/core'; import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser'; import {provideRouter, withExperimentalPlatformNavigation} from '@angular/router'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: ` Download report.csv
`, }) class App {} bootstrapApplication(App, { providers: [provideRouter([{path: '**', children: []}], withExperimentalPlatformNavigation())], }); ``` In Chrome, clicking the link changes the URL to `/report.csv` and nothing is downloaded. Submitting the form changes the URL to `/submit`, and the server never gets the POST. The download case can also be seen live on https://next.angular.dev/ai/develop-with-ai. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true No error. Both become SPA navigations. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular 22.2.1 in Chrome 155, and next.angular.dev (22.3.0-next.2+sha-16932e9). 22.2.3 ships the same check. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): separate class compilation and emission into two passes
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #71477 suggested by @crisbeto (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71477#discussion_r4333629455).

Separates class processing in `processFileSync` into two explicit passes:
1. **Compilation pass:** Compiles all class decorators (`@Pipe`, `@Component`, `@Directive`, `@Service`, `@Injectable`, `@NgModule`) and metadata statements into `CompiledClass` AST records so `sharedPool` (`ConstantPool`) finalizes all `FixupExpression`s across the file. `compileNgModuleDef` now returns compiled ASTs (`CompiledNgModuleDef`) rather than printing inline.
2. **Emission pass:** Prints and appends static fields and trailing statements for each `CompiledClass` via `appendCompiledClass`, eliminating the `deferredClassAppends` closure array and deduplicating `createStaticField` calls.

This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`11.28.5` → `11.28.7`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/11.28.5/11.28.7) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/11.28.7?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/11.28.7?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/11.28.5/11.28.7?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/11.28.5/11.28.7?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.7`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.7): pnpm 11.28.7 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.6...v11.28.7) This release rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested, applies `trustPolicy` to the pnpm version a project pins, and caps unpacked package size with `maxTarballUnpackedSize`. It also removes support for registry revisions, fixes `verifyDepsBeforeRun` after filtered installs, and finishes commands with their own exit code when a pipe reader exits early. ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NAME_MISMATCH` if a registry returns metadata for a package other than the one requested. Before, pnpm installed the package under the name in the metadata, so `allowBuilds` rules for the requested package did not apply to it. - pnpm now applies `trustPolicy` to the pnpm version a project pins in `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager`. A pinned version whose trust evidence was downgraded fails the command before pnpm switches to it or records it in the lockfile [#​16319](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16319). - `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune` and `trustPolicyExcludePrune` now keep exclusions for resolved configuration dependencies and their transitive dependencies [#​17142](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17142). - Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. `pnpm install` fails with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_TOO_LARGE` when the files of one package unpack to more than this many bytes, 4 GiB by default [pnpm/tasks#81](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/81). ##### Resolving dependencies - Registry revisions are no longer supported. pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_REVISIONS_UNSUPPORTED` on registry metadata that selects a revision, on a `+rN` version specifier, and on a lockfile entry with a `revision` field. `pnpm update --patches` is removed. - When `pnpm install` resolves a dependency again, it now reuses a version that the install already resolved for the same package, as a fresh install does. Before, it kept the version the lockfile pinned and added a second copy of the package. A locked version still stays when nothing else in the install prefers another version. To pin a transitive dependency on purpose, use `overrides` [#​17084](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17084). - When another workspace project adds a different version of a package, a project's auto-installed peer on that package now moves to the version a fresh install picks. It used to stay on its locked version while any other project still accepted that version [#​17058](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17058). - An optional peer that pnpm adds to a project now keeps the version the lockfile recorded for that project only while the dependency graph still holds it. Otherwise it follows its provider to a version the graph holds. Before, pnpm kept a higher version that only the lockfile held, which left two copies of the peer [#​16443](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16443). - A package that lists the same dependency in `dependencies` and as an optional peer now gets the peer bound when a project adds a provider for it later. The lockfile now records every peer a package declares, including one its own dependency supplies [#​17056](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17056). - `pnpm install --prod` no longer drops a dependency that a package declares both as an optional peer and as its own dependency, when the package resolved it as its own dependency and a dev dependency provides the same package under another alias. - pnpm now measures a `pnpm.overrides` entry written as a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, from the directory holding `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. It used to be measured from each package the override rewrote. The install then linked a directory that does not exist, or failed if workspace packages were injected [#​17010](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17010). - `pnpm install` now removes config dependencies that are no longer declared, including when the entire `configDependencies` setting is removed. Frozen installs reject a lockfile that still records removed config dependencies. - `pnpm add` now reads the package name correctly from a tarball URL under a registry URL that has a path, such as `https://example.com/npm/`. Before, the registry path became part of the name, so a scoped package failed with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_PACKAGE_NAME`. - `pnpm add` no longer warns that a gist dependency was replaced from a different source when the new specifier names the same gist in another form, such as `gist:` and `https://gist.github.com//`. - With `minimumReleaseAge` set, pnpm now revalidates a package's cached full metadata with a single ETag request so an unchanged registry answers with `304`, and keeps using the cached copy once the registry confirms it is current, even when the metadata does not list a publish time for every version. Previously, pnpm downloaded that metadata again whenever the cached copy was older than `minimumReleaseAge`. Packages listed in `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` also resolve from cached metadata without a registry request when the lockfile already has the version their range picks. ##### Linking node_modules and workspaces - Concurrent installs that import the same package into one project now all complete. One of them used to fail with `ENOTEMPTY` when its copy of the package collided with the copy another install had already placed [pnpm/tasks#48](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/48). - `pnpm install` no longer fails on macOS with `EISDIR` when it creates store directories in a group-writable store under a umask that removes owner read, such as `0o477`. - `pnpm install` now succeeds when `node_modules` is a symlink to an existing directory. Dependency hoisting previously rejected a symlinked `node_modules` as an invalid destination [#​17157](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17157). - A filtered `pnpm install --no-lockfile` with `hoistWorkspacePackages` now hoists every workspace project into `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules`. It used to hoist only the selected projects [pnpm/tasks#168](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/168). - Filtered installs remove obsolete dependencies from the installed lockfile while preserving dependencies still needed by unselected projects. - With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` now runs the `preResolution` hooks and custom resolvers and fetchers of the workspace root's pnpmfile for every project, next to the project's own. A global pnpmfile now runs once per project, and each project's lockfile records the checksum of the root pnpmfile when the project has none of its own. Before, a project's own pnpmfile replaced these root hooks, the global hooks ran twice, and edits to the root pnpmfile could go unnoticed. - `pnpm prune` now removes extraneous direct packages from `node_modules` when `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are already in sync. `pnpm prune` also accepts `--filter` and `--recursive` to prune selected workspace projects without removing dependencies of unselected projects. ##### Injected workspace packages - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` when the dependencies of an injected workspace package or local directory dependency no longer match the lockfile. This covers `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` [#​17008](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17008), a dependency changed to a different tarball URL or git commit [#​17129](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17129), and a change in a transitive injected or local directory dependency [#​17128](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17128). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` when an injected workspace package depends on a local directory under another name, such as `"renamed": "file:../b"` [#​17130](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17130). - An injected workspace dependency now becomes a link when its dependencies match the workspace package's own, also on an install that leaves the package's installed dependencies as they are. Before, such an install kept it as a copy [#​17094](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17094). - An injected workspace package that was linked now becomes a copy when the project that depends on it starts providing one of its peers at a version the package's own workspace context lacks. The link used to stay until that dependency was updated, so the package could not find the peer the project provides [#​17057](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17057). - An injected workspace package now keeps only the files its manifest lists after a lifecycle script or a script named in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` rebuilds it. Before, these refreshes copied every file of the package directory into the injected copy, including files that `files` or `.npmignore` leave out. With `deployAllFiles: true` the copy still gets every file. - A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` now keeps a package's links to its own files as links in the injected copies, the way `pnpm install` writes them. It no longer fails when the package links to one directory twice or links back to a directory above the link. `pnpm install` with `deployAllFiles` no longer fails on such a link back either. - A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` now updates the injected copies of the package it ran in when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` or the package publishes from `publishConfig.directory`. Before, those copies kept the files from the last install. ##### Running scripts and checking dependencies - When the reader of pnpm's output exits early, as in `pnpm outdated | head`, pnpm now finishes the command and exits with the command's own exit code [pnpm/tasks#133](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/133). It used to exit with code 0 at the first write to the closed pipe. That hid the result of commands such as `pnpm outdated` and stopped `pnpm clean` before it removed anything. - With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, a Node.js resolve hook that a script registers now sees the importer as `context.parentURL` after pnpm's `NODE_PATH` fallback fails to find a bare specifier. Hooks that resolve tsconfig `paths` aliases from the importer failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` [#​16979](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16979). - `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, and `pnpm restart` now pass the install flags they were given, such as `--lockfile-dir`, `--modules-dir`, `--store-dir`, `--offline`, and `--ignore-scripts`, to the `pnpm install` that `verifyDepsBeforeRun: install` starts. When that install leaves `node_modules` out of date, pnpm now prints a warning. - After `pnpm install --filter`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now notice a changed manifest or lockfile in a project that the filtered install left out, including the workspace root after a filtered install with `pruneDirectDependencies: true` [pnpm/tasks#181](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/181). A filtered install also preserves the recorded ignored build scripts of unselected projects, and `pnpm dedupe --check` and `pnpm install --dry-run` no longer record outdated dependencies as installed. - The `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check now holds the workspace projects that the selected project depends on, including `link:` workspace dependencies. `--filter=...` now selects `link:` dependencies as well. With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` also reports dependencies as outdated when a selected project's `pnpm-lock.yaml` is missing [pnpm/tasks#138](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/138). - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` and repeat `pnpm install` runs now apply `overrides` before comparing a modified `package.json` with `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#​17127](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17127). `verifyDepsBeforeRun` also checks whether each importer's resolved catalog versions match the catalog snapshot in `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and respects `lockfileDir` in single-project repositories. - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now compares manifests, lockfiles, and patch files by content hash. It notices an edit that kept the file's modification time, as `cp -p`, `rsync -a`, or an archive extraction leave it, and a patch file that was copied or touched without changing its content no longer marks dependencies as outdated [#​16988](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16988). ##### Deploying and other commands - `pnpm deploy` now records the peer dependencies of the workspace packages it copies into the deployed lockfile. Before, pnpm rejected that lockfile with `--frozen-lockfile` when a deployed workspace package declared a peer and `injectWorkspacePackages` was off [#​17093](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17093). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now succeed inside a directory created by `pnpm deploy`. `pnpm deploy` writes self-contained workspace and lockfile settings, prunes unused `patchedDependencies`, and preserves workspace-level dependency resolutions on deployed directory dependencies. - In workspaces with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm patch`, `pnpm patch-commit`, and `pnpm patch-remove` now resolve patch files and `patchedDependencies` entries at the workspace root. `pnpm install` checks configured patches across all workspace projects before reporting unused patches. - Trusted publishing with OIDC now works with registries whose URL has a path, such as `https://registry.example/npm/private/`. pnpm previously sent the token exchange request to the root of the registry host. - `pnpm owner ls` now lists the owners of a package on the npm registry. It reported every package as not found. - `pnpm sbom` now reads project lockfiles in workspaces with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, including filtered and split output, and reports the repository of a package whose `repository` field is a `gist:` shorthand. - `pnpm licenses list` reports no licenses for workspace projects not recorded in the lockfile. It errors when `pnpm-lock.yaml` is missing. Empty results now use the requested text or JSON format [pnpm/tasks#174](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/174). - `pnpm why` now reads each selected workspace project's lockfile and modules directory when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#169](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/169). - `pnpm pkg fix` now converts a `repository` string such as `github:pnpm/example` to the object form, as `npm pkg fix` does. It also normalizes a GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repository URL the way `npm pkg fix` does [#​16980](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16980). ##### Configuration and setting up pnpm - pnpm now recognizes `externalDependencies` and `autoInstallPeersFromHighestMatch` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` without warning and forwards both settings to `pnpm install`. Previously, setting `externalDependencies` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` crashed `pnpm install` with `externalDependencies.has is not a function` [pnpm/tasks#166](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/166). - pnpm now ignores a `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variable for a URL setting, such as `PNPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, when its value is not a URL. Such a value used to make every command fail with `Invalid URL`. - The warning about unrecognized settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the global `config.yaml` now names `addMissingPeerTypes`, `autoDedupe`, `bootConfig`, `macosBackup`, `nodePackageMap`, `permissions`, `pipelineBase`, `publishWaitTimeout`, `python`, `remoteCache`, `saveTypes`, `skills`, `storeIndexFormat`, and `tools` as pnpm v12 settings [pnpm/tasks#167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/167). - When a config file has a setting pnpm cannot read, `pnpm --version` now prints the version, and `pmOnFail` and `lockfileDir` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` stay in force. Previously, pnpm switched to the pinned version despite `pmOnFail: ignore`. pnpm also no longer writes the pinned version to `pnpm-lock.yaml` when it cannot read every setting and the running pnpm already matches the pin. - pnpm now records the pinned pnpm version in the `pnpm-lock.yaml` under the `lockfileDir` set in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and resolves a relative `lockfileDir` from the workspace root. pnpm used to write a second `pnpm-lock.yaml` at the workspace root. - `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it. The global pnpm is left alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). - `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167). - `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973). ##### Platinum Sponsors

### [`v11.28.6`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.6): pnpm 11.28.6 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.5...v11.28.6) This release stops `pnpm publish` from sending a CI identity token to a registry it was not issued for. It also fixes installs that dropped a dependency also declared as an optional peer, and accepts empty `httpProxy` and `httpsProxy` settings again. ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - `pnpm publish` now uses an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` only if its `aud` claim matches the selected registry, such as `npm:registry.npmjs.org`. A token for another registry is skipped with a warning, and pnpm falls back to the configured credentials. - The warning about renamed package files with invalid names no longer prints control characters from those file names. ##### Configuration - pnpm again accepts `httpProxy` and `httpsProxy` set to `null` or written with no value in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the global config file, and treats them as unset. Since 11.28.5 these values failed with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING`. - pnpm now switches to the pnpm version a project pins even when it cannot read its configuration. Previously, a setting it rejected in the global config file, an `.npmrc` file, `_auth`, or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` stopped every command, `pnpm --version` included. - A key under a registry URL in the `_auth` setting that does not start with `@` is now skipped with a warning, so a field a later pnpm version adds there no longer breaks this one. A key that holds an `authToken` object but lacks its `@`, such as `org` for `@org`, is still an error. ##### Resolving dependencies - pnpm no longer drops a dependency that a package also declares as an optional peer dependency, for example `ajv` of `ajv-formats`. Since 11.28.0, in some dependency graphs the package got the dependency neither as a dependency nor as a peer, and failed to import it [#​16901](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16901). - `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION` after a change to `overrides` when the lockfile resolves an optional peer dependency to an npm alias of another package [#​16654](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16654). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now link an optional peer to the workspace package that the workspace root depends on when the picked version matches it. Previously they installed the registry package with the same name and version [#​16706](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16706). - Removal overrides such as `"debug>supports-color": "-"` now also apply to an optional peer that a package declares only in `peerDependenciesMeta` [#​16681](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16681). - `pnpm dedupe` now preserves a hoisted workspace package when another package uses a separately installed peer with the same name [#​16935](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16935). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm add --config` now apply `minimumReleaseAge` when they resolve a config dependency. A config dependency range resolves to the newest version that is old enough, so a later clean `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepts the lockfile [#​16660](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16660). - `pnpm install --fix-lockfile` no longer removes the `deprecated` and `hasBin` fields from lockfile entries [#​6600](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6600). ##### Workspaces and catalogs - A filtered install, such as `pnpm install --filter `, now keeps the `pnpm-lock.yaml` entries of workspace projects that are missing from disk, as in a sparse checkout. Their importers, packages, and catalog entries stay even when the filter matches every project on disk [#​16931](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16931). - `catalogPrune` no longer removes catalog entries that `pnpm-lock.yaml` still records for workspace projects missing from disk. This affected `pnpm remove` and installs that leave the lockfile unchanged, such as frozen installs. Before, a following frozen install failed with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` [#​16679](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16679). - Sped up workspace discovery with subtree exclusions such as `!generated/**`. ##### Linking node_modules - `pnpm install` no longer fails on Windows with `EPERM` on `rmdir node_modules/@scope` when several workspace packages under one scope are hoisted, for example with `nodeLinker: hoisted` [#​16690](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16690). - `pnpm install` hardlinks files from a group-writable or world-writable store again. Before this fix, pnpm copied every file from such a store into `node_modules` [#​16677](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16677). - With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, an install that updates `node_modules` now restores the dependency links of a package in the global virtual store that an interrupted install left without them. Before, such an install kept the incomplete package if the project's `node_modules` already recorded it [#​16642](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16642). - Removing a `link:` dependency now also removes its symlink from `node_modules` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​16884](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16884). - An install that adds nothing to the store no longer changes the modification time of the store directory. CI caches that check modification times, such as GitLab's, no longer re-upload an unchanged store [#​16929](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16929). ##### Injected workspace packages - With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, an injected workspace package installed in the same run as its dependent now holds only the files its `files` field selects. The copy used to also hold other files of the project, such as `tsconfig.json` [#​16683](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16683). - A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` no longer fails when it rewrites `package.json` while pnpm is copying its edits into the injected copies. The sync after the script now replaces a half-copied manifest. - Sped up frozen installs of unchanged injected workspace packages that use hardlinks. ##### Deploying - `pnpm deploy` without `injectWorkspacePackages` now binds a peer dependency of a linked workspace package to the version its parent provides, as an injected install does. Previously the deploy failed with `ERR_PNPM_DEPLOY_AMBIGUOUS_PEER` whenever other packages in the deployed graph depended on different versions of that peer [#​16807](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16807). - `pnpm deploy` in a workspace with `injectWorkspacePackages` no longer crashes when a linked workspace package declares a peer dependency named after an `Object.prototype` member, such as `constructor`. ##### Setting up pnpm - pnpm now relinks the bins of a pnpm version it installed earlier for `packageManager` or `pnpm with`. A pnpm 12 version installed by a pnpm release older than 11.28.4 could keep a launcher that ran `node` on the native binary, so every command failed with `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token` [#​16646](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16646). - `pnpm setup` no longer tries to install pnpm globally from npm's `bin` directory when pnpm was installed with npm. It printed `Failed to create bin at /bin/pnpm` [#​16855](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16855). ##### Output - Escape codes in script output that moved the cursor or cleared the screen garbled pnpm's output. pnpm now drops them and keeps only color codes. Color codes are dropped too when pnpm's own output is not in color. - When the registry rejects `pnpm stage publish`, the error message now starts with "Failed to stage package". ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors

Issues.Title: build: update dependency rules_nodejs to v6.7.7 (22.2.x)
Issues.Body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [rules_nodejs](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_nodejs) | bazel_dep | patch | `6.7.6` → `6.7.7` |

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>bazel-contrib/rules_nodejs (rules_nodejs)</summary>

### [`v6.7.7`](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_nodejs/releases/tag/v6.7.7)

#### Using Bzlmod with Bazel 6 or greater

1. (Bazel 6 only) Enable with `common --enable_bzlmod` in `.bazelrc`.
2. Add to your `MODULE.bazel` file:

```starlark
bazel_dep(name = "rules_nodejs", version = "6.7.7")
```

#### Using WORKSPACE

Paste this snippet into your `WORKSPACE.bazel` file:

```starlark
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")
http_archive(
    name = "rules_nodejs",
    sha256 = "f87453e0d6a97b4d2e6d22070a447b6d304727bf61ff8e31ce25ded0319005dd",
    strip_prefix = "rules_nodejs-6.7.7",
    url = "https://github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_nodejs/releases/download/v6.7.7/rules_nodejs-v6.7.7.tar.gz",
)
```

#### What's Changed

- Update Node.js Versions by [@​mattem](https://redirect.github.com/mattem) in [#​3927](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_nodejs/pull/3927)

- chore: add acozzette to BCR maintainers by [@​acozzette](https://redirect.github.com/acozzette) in [#​3934](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/rules_nodejs/pull/3934)

microsoft/playwright (playwright-core) ### [`v1.64.1`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.64.1) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/compare/v1.64.0...v1.64.1) ##### Bug Fixes - [#​43247](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/43247) \[Bug]: \_electron.launch intermittently loses a packaged app's first window since 1.64.0 - [#​43242](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/43242) \[Regression]: Chromium 155+ aborts a preflighted cross-origin redirect whenever any route is registered (net::ERR_ABORTED)
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.15.0): pnpm 12.15 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.14.0...v12.15.0) This release lets `pnpm-workspace.yaml` delegate settings to other files and config dependencies with `include`, adds `lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` and tar-registry support, accepts zstd-compressed registry responses, and honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install`. It also rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested and speeds up workspace installs and macOS file linking. ##### Minor Changes - `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new `include` field. Each source may define only the settings the root manifest delegates to it. Every setting has one owner. Commands that change settings write each one to the file that owns it. A relative path in an included file is relative to that file. See [Splitting Settings Across Files](https://pnpm.io/config-includes). A config dependency supplies its settings through the YAML file named in the `pnpm.config` field of its `package.json`. The new `bootConfig` setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies and the pnpm version from `packageManager`. - Added the `lockfile.integrityTarget` setting. With `integrityTarget: tar`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins the hash of every package's uncompressed tar, so the lockfile no longer changes when a registry recompresses its tarballs or serves them as tars. pnpm learns a version's tar hash from the store or by downloading it once. `pnpm audit signatures` ties the tar hash to the signed `.tgz` integrity. ```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml" lockfile: integrityTarget: tar ``` - pnpm can now install from a registry that serves uncompressed tars with zstd or gzip content coding. `pnpm-l > [!IMPORTANT] > ✂ PR body was truncated to here.
--- ### Configuration and setting up pnpm - Registry credentials and TLS settings passed with `--config`, such as `--config.//registry.example.com/:_authToken=`, are now applied. They take precedence over the same settings in `.npmrc` files. - pnpm now reads only the settings it needs to decide whether to switch to the pnpm version a project pins. A setting outside them can no longer fail that decision or change its outcome. For example, `pnpm --version` no longer fails in a pinned project whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a setting this pnpm cannot read. Projects that pin neither pnpm nor a runtime skip this check without reading any settings. - When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, an option only the pinned pnpm knows now reaches that pnpm when it comes immediately before the command name, as in `pnpm --new-flag install`. When switching for `pnpm --version` or an unrecognized command line, pnpm also honors `--color`, `--no-color`, `--reporter`, and `--loglevel` wherever they appear on the command line. - `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it, leaving the global pnpm alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). Run inside a workspace package, `pnpm self-update` updates the pin in the workspace root's manifest, including in `package.yaml` or `package.json5`. - `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167). - `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973). - In StackBlitz WebContainers, `pnpm` no longer crashes intermittently with `Parking not supported on this platform`, and running a command that does not exist now reports that the command was not found. Previously it sometimes failed with a generic error. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.14.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.14.0): pnpm 12.14.0 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.13.0...v12.14.0) This release adds the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting, stops `pnpm install` from waiting on the daily update check, and keeps pnpm from aborting with a core dump when the reader of its output exits. ##### Minor Changes - Added the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting for packages whose build depends on something pnpm cannot include in the cache key, such as the system libraries a native addon links against. pnpm builds the listed packages in every project and never restores or saves their builds through the side-effects cache, locally or on a `remoteCache` server. Under the global virtual store, each project gets its own copy of these packages and of the packages that depend on them. Entries use the same `name`, `@scope/*`, and `name@version` patterns as `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` [#​5271](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5271). - `pnpm login` now prints the `npm-notice` response header during web-based login. Registries use it to show the verification code that completes the sign-in in the browser. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` no longer wait for the daily update check. If the command finishes first, pnpm skips the update notice and checks again next time. On a registry that accepted the connection but never answered, an install that had nothing to do used to take minutes [#​16839](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839). - `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` and `pnpm update` now reuse `pnpm-lock.yaml` when the workspace configures a catalog entry that no dependency references, such as an unused entry or one whose package an `overrides` entry replaces. Before, every resolution in such a workspace resolved all dependencies again from the registry [#​16923](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16923). - `pnpm install` now looks up a git dependency's branch or tag once per install, even when many workspace projects depend on it. With `linkWorkspacePackages` enabled, it used to run `git ls-remote` once per project [#​16899](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16899). - A filtered install, such as `pnpm install --filter `, now keeps the `pnpm-lock.yaml` entries of workspace projects that are missing from disk, as in a sparse checkout. Their importers, packages, and catalog entries stay even when the filter matches every project on disk [#​16931](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16931). - pnpm now decides whether a dependency that a package also declares as an optional peer is linked as a dependency or as a peer from the shallowest path that reaches the package. When an existing lockfile records such a dependency as a regular dependency and a newly added dependency now provides the peer, pnpm records it as a peer, as a fresh install does. The lockfile entry of such a package can change on the next install [#​16901](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16901). - An install that adds nothing to the store no longer changes the modification time of the store directory. CI caches that check modification times, such as GitLab's, no longer re-upload an unchanged store [#​16929](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16929). ##### Running commands and scripts - pnpm no longer aborts with a core dump when the reader of its output has exited, as in `pnpm list | head -1` or `pnpm start 2>&1 | head -1`. The command finishes with its usual exit code, and a failing script's exit code is kept. A write to stdout that fails for another reason, such as a full disk, ends the command with exit code 1 [#​16904](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16904) [pnpm/tasks#132](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/132). - On Windows, `pnpm exec`, `pnpm run`, and commands such as `pnpm nx` now return when the command they run exits, even if it left a detached process running and pnpm's output is redirected or piped. Previously a shell reading that output waited until the detached process, such as the Nx daemon, exited [#​16930](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16930). - Commands that do not write the project manifest now leave a missing `package.json` absent. This covers queries such as `pnpm why` and `pnpm outdated`, `pnpm fetch`, `pnpm dedupe --check`, and commands that exit with an error, such as `pnpm rt ls`. These commands used to create one from the initialization template. `pnpm sbom` run from a lockfile alone now reports the root component as `unknown` with version `0.0.0` [#​16907](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16907). - `pnpm run` now reports a failed script as a JSON record under `--reporter=ndjson`. It printed a plain `[ELIFECYCLE]` line to stderr. - `pnpm run` no longer prints `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code N.` to stderr when a script fails under `--reporter=silent`, `--silent`, or `--loglevel=silent`. - `pnpm pipeline --dry-run` no longer writes a run report when no projects are selected. With `--json` it prints `{"tasks": []}` [pnpm/tasks#126](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/126). ##### Packing and publishing - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now ship the whole gitignored directory that `main`, `browser`, or `bin` points into, as npm does. Previously only the `main` and `bin` files themselves were packed, and a gitignored `browser` file was left out [#​16908](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16908). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now honor a `.npmignore` or `.gitignore` inside a subdirectory when `package.json` has a `files` field. The package root's ignore files and those inherited from the workspace are still skipped [#​16909](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16909). ##### Setting up pnpm and toolchains - `--registry`, `--https-proxy`, `--http-proxy`, and `--no-proxy` now apply when pnpm resolves and downloads the pnpm version a project pins in `packageManager`. Before, these lookups went to `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, which a firewall that only allows a private registry blocks [#​16911](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/16911). - On Windows, `pnpm install` now installs the Rust toolchain for rustup's default host, so a machine set up with `rustup set default-host x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` gets the MinGW toolchain. Without a default host, pnpm installs the MSVC toolchain for the machine's architecture, as rustup does. This includes a pnpm built for MinGW, such as the MSYS2 package, which has installed the MinGW toolchain since 12.13.0. An x64 pnpm on ARM64 Windows now installs the ARM64 toolchain [#​16854](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16854). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.13.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.13.0): pnpm 12.13.0 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.12.1...v12.13.0) This release adds the `pnpm profile` and `pnpm token` commands, the `storeIndexFormat: files` setting for stores shared over a network filesystem, and faster Python dependency resolution. ##### Minor Changes - Added the `pnpm profile` command to view and update registry user profile settings. - Added `pnpm token` to list, create, and revoke authentication tokens on the registry. - Added the `storeIndexFormat` setting. Set it to `files` to keep a store's package index as one file per package instead of the SQLite `index.db`, for a store on a network filesystem that several machines use at once. SQLite's locking does not work across machines, so concurrent installs on such a store could corrupt `index.db`. - Added the `nodePackageMap` setting, which groups the package-map settings. `nodePackageMap.mode: write-only` writes `node_modules/.package-map.json` for other tools without making Node.js load it. `mode: load` also makes Node.js load the map, like `nodeExperimentalPackageMap: true`. `nodePackageMap.type` replaces `nodePackageMapType`. The old settings still work [#​14937](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14937). ```yaml nodePackageMap: mode: write-only type: loose ``` ##### Patch Changes ##### Setting up pnpm - `pnpm setup` now works when pnpm was installed with npm on macOS. It installed pnpm from npm's `bin` directory and left a `$PNPM_HOME/bin/pnpm` that could not run [#​16855](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16855). - pnpm runs again after `pnpm setup` when `globalShims` enables pnpm. Every command failed with "the global target of the pnpm shim points back at the shim" [#​16874](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16874). - A pnpm built for the MinGW target on Windows, such as the MSYS2 package, now installs the MinGW Rust toolchain that `rust-toolchain.toml` names. It used to install the MSVC toolchain. ##### Installing packages - On macOS, `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_WRITE_FILE` when the project is on a virtiofs or SMB share. pnpm now falls back to a regular `fsync` when the file system rejects a full sync [#​16846](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16846). - On macOS, `pnpm install`, `pnpm patch-commit`, and other commands that load a pnpmfile no longer hang at random. - `pnpm install` now puts the executables of a Python build backend's requirements on the `PATH` while the backend runs. Projects built with `uv_build` now install. Before, they failed with "uv-build was not properly installed". - Removing a `link:` dependency now also removes its symlink from `node_modules` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​16884](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16884). - `pnpm-lock.yaml` no longer records the tarball URL of a package installed from a scoped registry, such as one set by `@types:registry=`, when pnpm can rebuild the URL from that registry [#​16866](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16866). ##### Packing, auditing, and pipelines - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now pack only `package.json`, the README, the license, and the files named in `main` and `bin` when `files` is an empty array. They used to pack every file in the package [#​16889](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16889). - `pnpm audit` and `pnpm audit signatures` no longer check runtimes installed through `devEngines.runtime`, such as `node@runtime:24.21.0`, against the npm package of the same name. `pnpm audit signatures` reported these runtimes as having an invalid registry signature [#​16869](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16869). - `pnpm pipeline` now runs the root's tasks when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists only the root in `packages` or omits `packages`, as `pnpm -r run` does. A change to a root file in such a workspace no longer triggers a full-run warning. When a full run has no projects to run, `pnpm pipeline` now reports that no projects are selected [#​16849](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16849). ##### Performance - `pnpm install` resolves Python dependencies faster. With `--lockfile-only`, a project with 10 dependencies now resolves in about 4 seconds, down from about 40. When the index publishes a metadata file beside each wheel (PEP 658), as PyPI does, pnpm downloads only the wheels of the releases it selects. - A repeat install against an existing lockfile no longer reads registry metadata for the dependencies it takes from that lockfile. On a warm store this removes thousands of metadata lookups from a repeat install of a large workspace. - `pnpm install` with `enableModulesDir: false` now verifies the packages already in the store while the dependencies resolve, and checks a package's files in parallel. On a 5,100-package install with the store on a network filesystem, this removed a 19-second pause between resolution and fetching. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors

A token for another registry is skipped with a warning, and pnpm falls back to the configured credentials. - `pnpm dist-tag add`, `rm`, and `ls` now support OIDC authentication in CI. Enable "Allow npm dist-tag" in the package's trusted publishing settings to manage tags without a stored npm token. - Added the `tool:` protocol for the tools pnpm downloads itself: Node.js, Bun, Deno, and Yarn. `pnpm add bun@tool:1.3.0`, `pnx node@tool:22`, and `pnx yarn@tool:4` work like the `runtime:` spelling, which stays supported as an alias. Issues.Title: fix(core): clear jsaction cache when removing event listeners
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #71545

After event replay, `removeListeners` drops the `jsaction` attribute and the stashed listeners, but the parsed action map that the event contract's `ActionResolver` caches on the element as `__jsaction` stays. With incremental hydration the event contract is still alive after the app is stable, so a later click on an element that was replayed earlier resolves the stale map, finds an action and calls `preventDefault()`. A link like `<a target="_blank">` that got an early click can then no longer be opened.

## What is the new behavior?

`removeListeners` also clears the cached action map, so the next click re-reads the element, finds no action and keeps the browser default.

- `packages/core/primitives/event-dispatch` exports the existing cache `clear` helper as `clearActionCache`, next to `getActionCache`. The public API golden and the hydration bundle symbols golden are updated.
- `event_replay_spec.ts` gets a test: after an early click on a link is replayed, a second click is not default-prevented.
- The language service mock typings (`primitives-event-dispatch.d.ts` in both test workspaces) export `clearActionCache` too, to match the entry point.

Fixes #71545

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

## Other information

No docs change: the fix is internal; the only new export is in the event-dispatch primitives entry point.

### Verification

Run locally on macOS (Bazel 8.8.2), logs: https://gist.github.com/fixfon/0ba71a4db6f9e08913aa1df056670d0d

- `//packages/platform-server/test:event_replay_test`: 25 specs, 0 failures. With the core change reverted, the new test is the only failure (`Expected true to be false.`).
- `//packages/core:core_api` and `//packages/core/test/bundling/hydration:symbol_test`: pass.
- `prettier --check` on the changed core and test files: pass.
- The wider platform-server test suite and the event-dispatch unit tests: not run, CI will cover.
- Language service fixtures: fixture updated, test not run locally; the export list was compared by hand with `packages/core/primitives/event-dispatch/index.ts`.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): keep imports identical between local and optimized emit for @Inject params
Issues.Body:
If a constructor has a parameter like `@Inject(TOKEN) dep: ImportedType`, the preprocessor emitted different code depending on the compilation mode:

1. In local mode it was emitting `type: undefined` in `ɵsetClassMetadata`. Since there were no remaining value references, TS was dropping the import.
2. In optimized mode it kept the reference which caused TS to preserve it.

This ended up breaking an internal target. These changes fix the issue by making the cross-file pass respect the single-file decision.

Issues.Title: Event replay: early click leaves stale __jsaction cache, making prerendered target="_blank" links permanently unclickable
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? Don't known / other ### Is this a regression? Yes ### Description # Angular issue: an early click makes a prerendered `target="_blank"` link permanently unclickable (stale `__jsaction` cache) **Package:** `@angular/core` (event replay / incremental hydration) **Version:** 22.2.3 (reproduced on a fresh `ng new --ssr` project; first seen after upgrading an app from 19 to 22) **Browser:** Chrome (stable) ## Description With the v22 default `provideClientHydration()` (incremental hydration, which brings event replay), a prerendered `` that is clicked while event replay is still active becomes **permanently unclickable**. Every later click is `preventDefault()`ed by the event contract, even after Angular has removed the `jsaction` attribute. No new tab opens until the page is reloaded. Clicking only after the app is stable works. Using `withNoIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay()` also works. ## Minimal reproduction `ng new repro --ssr --routing --defaults` (Angular 22.2.3), then replace three files: `src/app/app.ts` ```ts import { Component, PendingTasks, inject } from '@angular/core'; import { RouterLink, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [RouterLink, RouterOutlet], template: ` Open /other in a new tab `, }) export class App { constructor() { // Stand-in for an HTTP request in flight after load: keeps the app unstable for 3 s. inject(PendingTasks).run(() => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000))); } } ``` `src/app/other.ts` ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-other', template: `

Other page

` }) export class Other {} ``` `src/app/app.routes.ts` ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; import { Other } from './other'; @Component({ selector: 'app-home', template: `

Home page

` }) class Home {} export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', component: Home }, { path: 'other', component: Other }, ]; ``` `app.config.ts` stays as generated: `provideClientHydration()`. Build (`ng build`, prerender), serve `dist/repro/browser` statically, open `/`. ## Steps 1. Within the first ~3 s (app bootstrapped, not yet stable), click "Open /other in a new tab". 2. Wait until the app is stable; the `jsaction` attribute disappears from the link. 3. Click the link again. **Expected:** step 3 opens `/other` in a new tab. **Actual:** nothing happens. The click is `preventDefault()`ed by the event contract; this repeats on every click until reload. Control cases (same app, real trusted clicks): | Configuration | Early click, then click at 6 s | Clicks only at 6 s and 8 s | |---|---|---| | `provideClientHydration()` (v22 default) | **6 s click: no tab** (`defaultPrevented=true`) | both open a tab | | `provideClientHydration(withNoIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay())` | both open a tab | both open a tab | Stack of the `preventDefault()` on the 6 s click (dev build): `Dispatcher.dispatch` → `EventDispatcher.dispatch` → `_EventContract.dispatcher` → `_EventContract.handleEventInfo` → `_EventContract.handleEvent` → listener on ``. ## Root cause (from the 22.2.3 sources) 1. On the early click, `ActionResolver.parseActions(element)` parses `jsaction="click:;"` and caches the parsed map **on the element** as the property `element.__jsaction` (`set(actionElement, actionMap)`). 2. When the block/app is cleaned up, `removeListeners(el)` does `el.removeAttribute('jsaction'); el.removeAttribute('ngb'); el.__jsaction_fns = undefined;` but it **does not clear `el.__jsaction`**. 3. With incremental hydration enabled, the `EventContract` is not cleaned up after `whenStable()`. `withEventReplay`'s bootstrap listener only calls `eventContract.cleanUp()` on app destroy when `isIncrementalHydrationEnabled`, so the `` listener stays active. 4. On every later click, `parseActions` returns the stale cached map, so an action is found. Because the element is an `` and the event is a click, `shouldPreventDefaultBeforeDispatching` returns true and the default (opening the new tab) is cancelled. RouterLink then leaves `target="_blank"` to the browser, so nothing navigates. Without the early click, `__jsaction` was never cached; after the attribute is removed `parseActions` sees no attribute, and the click is not prevented. With incremental hydration off, the contract is cleaned up at stable, so the stale cache is never consulted. Same-tab `routerLink`s mask the problem (RouterLink navigates itself after the default is prevented); any anchor that relies on the browser default (`target="_blank"`, plain `href` with a `(click)` listener, download links) is affected. ## Workaround we use An inline script at the end of `index.html` removes `jsaction` from `a[target="_blank"]` before any click, so these links are never intercepted or cached: ```html ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug _No response_ ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.3 Angular : 22.2.3 Node.js : 24.21.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 ``` ### Anything else? _No response_
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Event replay: early click leaves stale __jsaction cache, making prerendered target="_blank" links permanently unclickable" (#71545)

Issues.Title: Inconsistent behavior in processing query params Params across different router functions
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No (same on 21)

### Description

All related functions, to my knowledge, except `createUrlTreeFromSnapshot`, allow removing specific parameters from URLs by specifing their keys with null-ish value, eg.:

```
this.router.navigate(['./'], { queryParams: { hello: null } });
```

Above would remove "hello" query parameter when executed.

The `createUrlTreeFromSnapshot` however behaves differently:

```
 this.router.navigateByUrl(
    createUrlTreeFromSnapshot(this.activatedRoute.snapshot, [], {
      hello: null,
    })
  );
```

Above would set "hello" query parameter to "null" (so ?hello=null).

This is especially perplexing, given constructing URL tree manually works just fine:

```
this.router.navigateByUrl(
    this.router.createUrlTree(['/'], { queryParams: { hello: null } })
);
```

above would also clear the "hello" key.

https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-yphtdp7t?file=src%2Fmain.ts

Issues.Title: refactor(docs-infra): load doc content with router resources instead of resolvers
Issues.Body:
Enable `withRouterResources()` and load the content of docs, tutorial, CLI and API reference pages through a route `resources` function instead of a `docContent` resolver.

- Replace the `contentResolver()` helper from `@angular/docs` with `contentResource()`, which creates a `resource()` that loads the content through `DOCS_CONTENT_LOADER`. The resource stays idle with an `undefined` value when there is no content path, matching the previous resolver.
- `mapNavigationItemsToRoutes` now defines `resources` instead of `resolve` (keeping a `resources` function passed in the additional route properties). The content path is read from `ctx.data()` rather than captured in a closure: `ReuseTutorialsRouteStrategy` reuses the activated route between tutorial steps, which keeps the resources of the first step and only updates the route data, so reading it reactively makes the resource fetch the content of the new step.
- The CLI and API reference routes use `contentResource()` for their fixed content paths.

The resources are blocking, so the behavior is unchanged: navigation still waits for the content before activating the route (no loading state in the docs viewer, view transitions and prerendering see the full content), and the resolved value is bound to the existing `docContent` inputs. A failed load still fails the navigation with a `NavigationError`; the resource does not wrap `HttpErrorResponse` since it is error-like, so the navigation error handler keeps redirecting to `/404`. Query param only navigations (e.g. the API reference list filters) don't refetch, since the resource only tracks the content path.

This relies on the tutorial page reading its content from the `docContent` input, since resource values are not part of the route `data`.
